newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan hits 30-month high against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan hits 30-month high against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan hit a 30-month high during trading on Monday but closed down at an intra-day low of 8.2975 against the U.S. dollar on intervention by the central bank and follow-up selling, traders said.
On the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, the yuan opened unchanged from last Friday's 8.2970 and hit an intra-day high of 8.2950, a 30-month high.
It then fell to move between 8.2965 and 8.2970 for most of the session before closing at a low.
Trading was more active than last Friday, with most done at 8.2965, traders said.
"Active bids just after the opening pushed the yuan to its highest level since May 22, 1994, following gains last week," one dealer said.
"But the yuan's uptrend was halted by selling from the People's Bank of China," said a second dealer. "Some speculative offers at high levels also helped to cap its rise."
Dealers said the news that China would temporarily stop imports of some goods from USA as from mid-December had little impact on the yuan.
"If a trade war begins, demand for the dollar will fall and the yuan will gain solid support by the end of the year," a third trader said.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.2970 on Tuesday.
The yuan fell to close at 7.4450 from 7.3900 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0740 from 1.0738 against the Hong Kong dollar.
